## Summary
Implement the LOD brief generation step that uses Haiku to generate a ~200-token Level of Detail brief for each enriched SubConcept, stores it in Supabase `subconcept_lod_briefs`, and links the brief ID back to the SubConcept Neo4j node as a UUID FK only.

## User story
As a curriculum architect, I want each SubConcept to have a concise, clinically accurate LOD brief, so that assessment item generation has standardized context for question stem construction.

## Why this matters
This is a **CRITICAL (C07)** story. LOD briefs are the primary context source for downstream assessment generation. If stored as a Neo4j property (BANNED by Rule 7/AP-07), the graph becomes bloated with text data that degrades query performance. If generated with incorrect context (missing UMLS/anatomy/HetioNet data), the briefs will contain factual errors that propagate into student-facing questions — a FERPA and accreditation risk for MSM.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] LOD brief generated via HAIKU_MODEL (~200 tokens) using prompt from packages/ai/prompts/lod-brief.md
- [ ] Brief stored in Supabase `subconcept_lod_briefs` table (Rule 7)
- [ ] Neo4j SubConcept node updated with ONLY `lod_brief_id` UUID FK (NOT the brief text — AP-07)
- [ ] Supabase written FIRST, Neo4j updated SECOND (Rule 6)
- [ ] All Neo4j writes via neo4jQuery (Rule 1)
- [ ] Prompt uses sanitizeForContext + buildContextBlock (Rule 5)
- [ ] Claude response parsed with safeJsonParse (Rule 2)
- [ ] Model constant HAIKU_MODEL used (Rule 4)
- [ ] LRU cache (1000 entries) used for LOD facts lookup to avoid redundant DB reads
- [ ] Brief includes: definition, clinical significance, key relationships, common misconceptions
- [ ] Prompt template committed to packages/ai/prompts/lod-brief.md

## Canonical decisions in play
| Rule | What it means for this story |
|---|---|
| Rule 1 (C05) | neo4jQuery for SubConcept lod_brief_id update |
| Rule 2 (H06) | safeJsonParse for Haiku response — never raw JSON.parse |
| Rule 4 (D05) | HAIKU_MODEL constant — never hardcode model string |
| Rule 5 (H12) | sanitizeForContext + buildContextBlock + XML delimiters for lecture content |
| Rule 6 (G08) | Write brief to Supabase FIRST, then update Neo4j lod_brief_id |
| Rule 7 (G05/D12) | LOD brief text in Supabase subconcept_lod_briefs — NEVER as Neo4j property |
| AP-07 | lod_brief as Neo4j property is BANNED — only lod_brief_id UUID FK |

## Code patterns to follow
```typescript
// Pattern: LOD brief generation with Rule 7 compliance
import { neo4jQuery } from '@journey/neo4j/client';
import { createServerClient } from '@journey/db/server';
import { HAIKU_MODEL } from '@journey/ai/constants';
import { safeJsonParse } from '@journey/ai/safe-parse';
import { sanitizeForContext, buildContextBlock } from '@journey/ai/sanitize';
import { anthropic } from '@journey/ai/client';

export async function generateLodBrief(
  subconcept_id: string,
  institution_id: string,
  context: { umlsResult: UmlsResult; anatomyLinks: string[]; hetionetNodes: HetionetNode[] }
) {
  const supabase = createServerClient();

  // 1. Build sanitized context (Rule 5)
  const sanitizedContext = sanitizeForContext(JSON.stringify(context));
  const contextBlock = buildContextBlock('subconcept_enrichment', sanitizedContext);

  // 2. Generate brief with Haiku (Rule 4)
  const response = await anthropic.messages.create({
    model: HAIKU_MODEL, // Rule 4: constant, not hardcoded string
    max_tokens: 300,
    messages: [{ role: 'user', content: `${contextBlock}\n\nGenerate LOD brief...` }],
  });

  // 3. Parse response (Rule 2)
  const { data: brief } = safeJsonParse<LodBrief>(response.content[0].text);

  // 4. Supabase FIRST (Rule 6 + Rule 7)
  const { data: inserted } = await supabase
    .from('subconcept_lod_briefs')
    .upsert({
      subconcept_id,
      institution_id,
      brief_text: brief.text,        // Text lives HERE, not Neo4j
      token_count: brief.tokenCount,
      model_version: HAIKU_MODEL,
    })
    .select('id')
    .single();

  // 5. Neo4j SECOND — ONLY the UUID FK (Rule 7 / AP-07)
  await neo4jQuery(
    `MATCH (sc:SubConcept {uuid: $subconcept_id, institution_id: $inst})
     SET sc.lod_brief_id = $lod_brief_id`,
    { subconcept_id, inst: institution_id, lod_brief_id: inserted.id }
  );
  // NEVER: SET sc.lod_brief = $briefText ← AP-07 BANNED
}
```

## Code patterns to AVOID
```typescript
// ✗ AP-07: LOD brief as Neo4j property (BANNED — Rule 7)
SET sc.lod_brief = $briefText // BANNED — only lod_brief_id UUID FK allowed

// ✗ AP-02: Raw JSON.parse on Claude response (Rule 2)
const brief = JSON.parse(response.content[0].text); // BANNED — use safeJsonParse

// ✗ AP-03: Hardcoded model string (Rule 4)
model: 'claude-haiku-4-20250514' // BANNED — use HAIKU_MODEL constant

// ✗ AP-05: Unsanitized content in prompt (Rule 5)
const prompt = `Context: ${rawLectureText}`; // BANNED — use sanitizeForContext + buildContextBlock

// ✗ Rule 6: Neo4j before Supabase
await neo4jQuery(...); // WRONG ORDER
await supabase.from('subconcept_lod_briefs').insert(...);
```

## Rollback procedure
If implementation fails mid-way:
1. Supabase: `DELETE FROM subconcept_lod_briefs WHERE generated_at > '[timestamp]'`
2. Neo4j: `MATCH (sc:SubConcept) WHERE sc.lod_brief_id IS NOT NULL AND sc.p2_enriched_at > datetime('[timestamp]') SET sc.lod_brief_id = NULL`
3. git stash && git checkout develop
